current.title: Astronauts On The ISS See 16 Sunrises Every Day
current.hook: The station over your head is outrunning your last flight by 30 times.
current.closing: Even in space, you can't dodge a 24-hour day.
current.question: How many hours of daylight did you get today? Tell me below.

segments.topic: how fast the ISS orbits compared to a jet
segments.say: The ISS circles Earth at 27,600 kilometers an hour -- about 30 times faster than a commercial jet's 900. That speed isn't for show: it's exactly what keeps the station from falling into the ground.

segments.topic: why the ISS orbit period is so short
segments.say: So why so fast? Altitude decides orbital speed: the ISS orbits every 93 minutes, GPS satellites take 720, and geostationary satellites take a full 1,440 -- exactly matching Earth's spin.

segments.topic: how many sunrises the ISS sees in a day
segments.say: Each 93-minute lap flips the station from night to day, so a new sunrise comes every 93 minutes. On the ground that same cycle takes 1,440 minutes. Up there, it happens 16 times a day.

judge.one_line: The video never shows its own title: the '16 sunrises' payoff is replaced by a meaningless '1,347 apart' ruler, and the speed hook is two static numbers with duplicated mascots.
problems: hook/seg0: '900' vs '27.6K' as bare numbers with two copies of Data. The 30x speed is never shown as motion or distance, and the hook text is only captions.
hook/seg0 look the same for about 9s, so there's no progression.
seg1: the seesaw metaphor is wrong for orbital period, and GPS (720) disappears from the balance.
seg2: a bubble chart comparing 1440 and 93. No sunrise or orbit is drawn.
seg3/seg4: the ruler shows the difference (1,347), a meaningless number, and the headline '16 sunrises' is never visualised.
Truncated kicker in seg2. The mascot covers the jet label in seg0. The faded grey '1,347 apart' and the stacked labels are hard to read in seg4.
fixes: Hook: open with the ISS streaking around a small Earth while a jet crawls a tiny arc. Cover the same time window so the 30x gap reads as motion before any number appears.
seg1: draw three orbits at their altitudes (ISS inner, GPS middle, GEO outer) with satellites lapping at speeds scaled to 93, 720 and 1440, so the inner one laps fastest.
seg2/seg3: over one 24h ground clock, show the ISS completing laps and a sunrise flash at each terminator crossing, with a counter ticking 1…16. Data dons sunglasses at each one, faster and faster.
Replace the gap ruler with the 16 count as the final frame, and drop '1,347 apart'.
Give the kicker room so it isn't truncated, keep the mascot clear of labels, and make secondary labels full-contrast INK.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.
Each SAY is one spoken sentence or two, at most 40 words, and says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.

The HOOK is a 2000s download-site ad, not a fact read aloud: 6-14 words, the VIEWER is the one it happens to ('your coffee', 'your town'), lead with the shock, a visceral verb (wiped out, vanished, doubled, gone), one number from the data. Never a quiz ('Which animal...', 'Did you know...'), never a hedge (might, may, perhaps). Exaggerate the FEELING, never the FACT.

how_to_answer: Rewrite the WORDS so this story clears every rule above and answers every reason in `held_for`. Same number of segments, same order. Use ONLY numbers you can derive from each segment's `data.points` (or a year that appears as a label). If `judge` is present, its `problems`/`fixes` are what the video editor saw on the RENDERED video — shorter topics and one clear number per line are what fix 'unreadable' and 'text on text'. Write answer_path as one JSON object matching answer_schema, request_id and slug copied, and commit it. Do not touch the request.
